newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Oil firm Petronas looks at car engines.
newsitem.headline: Oil firm Petronas looks at car engines.

text.p: Malaysian oil firm Petronas said on Wednesday it will produce a passenger car engine with Switzerland's Sauber by June next year to spearhead its government's call for high-technology projects.
"We have to do that in order for the nation to get into high-tech business or the high-tech age," Petronas president Hassan Marican said.

"Otherwise one would have to keep relying on and buying technology developed by someone else," he told reporters after unveiling a new racing engine developed by Sauber for Petronas' Formula One team.
Malaysia has two national car companies, Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) and Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua). Both companies import engines made by the Japanese.
Proton's chassis are made by Mitsubishi while Perodua's are made by Daihatsu and Mitusi.

Hassan said Sauber Petronas Engineering A.G. -- a joint-venture firm in Switzerland owned 60 percent by Sauber and the balance by Petronas -- was now working on a prototype for a two-litre car engine to be launched in June 1998.
Hassan said once it took off, the project would involve Malaysians at all levels, from engineering to sales.
He also said it was almost inevitable the project would involve Proton, which has been unsuccessfully trying for more than 11 years to glean enough technology from Mitsubishi to make its own engines.
Proton and its late chairman Yahaya Ahmad bought Britain's Group Lotus Ltd last year to acquire the technology for manufacturing sports cars, after facing years of feet-dragging by Mitsubishi.

Hassan said it was still too early to give any figures on the financial or manufacturing aspects of the Petronas project, which grew out of the company's sponsorship and participation in Formula One races.
He added that Petronas had not decided yet whether to franchise the distribution rights for the engine.
"A lot of tests and acceptances are necessary before we can get into the commercial manufacturing of engines," he said.
Petronas president Azizan Zainul Abidin told a news conference earlier on Wednesday the company was considering the Asian market among options for its sales.
"A lot of people in Asia are assembling cars and we could be the producer and seller of their engines."
